title: Buccinator myomucosal flap for oral and oropharyngeal reconstruction: a series of 121 patients
html: Small-to-moderate oral and oropharyngeal defects can be repaired using various techniques, including primary closure, skin grafts, intraoral flaps, and extraoral flaps. Intraoral options include the buccal fat pad, palatal flap, tongue flap, and buccinator myomucosal flap (BMMF). Each flap has advantages and limitations in its applicability, due to anatomical and functional factors. This retrospective study evaluated 121 patients who underwent oral and oropharyngeal reconstruction using the BMMF; 102 had malignant tumours, two had benign tumours, 14 had cleft lip and palate, and three had oronasal/antral communications.
